Bottom line: One Atlantic system matters for Florida: Invest AL92 in the southwestern Gulf, near 100% (2-day) / near 100% (7-day). It is drifting slowly east now (NHC gives no speed). NHC expects it to turn north or northeast toward the northern Gulf Coast by the end of the week and says Florida Panhandle to Louisiana should closely monitor. Advisories are likely later today or tonight. No tropical watches or warnings anywhere in the US right now, including Tampa Bay.

4. Why and how they move

AL92 — slow east now, then north/northeast

  • Now: broad low in the SW Gulf, numerous moderate to strong thunderstorms 19–26N, 93–97W (TWDAT).
  • Setup (TWDAT): a front is stalled across the northern Gulf and into central Florida, with a surface trough from the front's tail down the Mexico coast to AL92. NHC has not yet published steering reasoning or a speed; its outlook only says the turn north or northeast comes by the end of the week.
  • Tampa angle: NHC's named zone is Panhandle to Louisiana. Tampa Bay is not in that wording, but with no track yet, keep watching.

Rachel — west, then sharp NE turn

  • How: W at 8 mph (275°/7 kt).
  • Why: steered by a subtropical ridge to the north; a mid/upper trough nearing the US West Coast weakens the ridge late week, so Rachel slows, turns sharply NE and speeds up (NHC Discussion 38).
  • Weakening: NE shear, drier stable air, water below 26°C within a day. Post-tropical by 96 h.
